limitations: declared_page_count is DOCX metadata, not a rendered page count

review.content_class_rationale: DOCX "SUPPLEMENTARY MATERIAL" with three non-clinical parts, all fully opened (text via pandoc, embedded Figure S1 EMF bitmap decoded and viewed): Table S1 sequencing read counts per sample (Total reads, Maintained reads, Reads processing, Percentage of maintained reads for Donor, Pre_FMT, M1, M4, M6), cited from the Methods as the read-depth check; Table S2 literature comparison of genera associated with IBS-C and IBS-C controls from reference (50) with approximate relative abundance in donor and recipient and an FMT-effect label; Figure S1 rarefaction curves (Number of ASVs versus read-count sample size, vertical lines at 150000 and 250000 reads, labelled Donor, Pre_FMT, M1, M4, M6). They are sequencing QC and genus-comparison material, not clinical measurements.

estimated_counts.basis: docx_xml peek table_row_count=27 across 2 tables (Table S1 header plus 5 sample rows; Table S2 header plus genus rows), confirmed by opening the full text; Figure S1 is one embedded bitmap

review.notes: Table S1 rows are named for the patient samples (Pre_FMT, M1, M4, M6) and the donor, and Table S2 gives approximate genus abundances in donor and recipient, but the content is library read depth and a literature comparison; no clinical value, diagnosis, date or treatment is carried. Classified as methods/QC background rather than patient-level clinical data; a reviewer who treats per-sample read counts as patient-level would need a clinical-data route.
limitations: The DOCX cannot be reviewed through the PDF/image supplement gates; classification rests on a full-text read plus a decoded copy of the single embedded Figure S1 EMF bitmap (no renderer for EMF is installed).
declared_page_count=2 is DOCX metadata, not a rendered page count.
No numeric values from the supplement are transcribed into any sidecar.
